Na czym opiera się procent szansy?: What is the chance percentage based on?
Dlaczego scenariusz z bliskim stopem nie: Why isn’t a scenario with a close stop green?
Przy każdej transakcji płacisz prowizję: Every trade costs fees and some slippage – about 0.2% in total for entry and exit. If the stop is e.g. 0.5% from the price, costs alone are 40% of what you risk. In the historical test half of the 24 h scenarios had a stop closer than 1.3% and came out clearly negative after costs, even though they were positive “on paper”. That is why only scenarios with a stop at least 1.3% from the price are green.
Który układ wybrać: 2:1, 1:1, 1:2 czy Au: Which setup to choose: 2:1, 1:1, 1:2 or Auto?
Sprawdziliśmy to na historii ok. 120 coi: We tested this on the history of about 120 coins (the TOP 10 at every moment, with fees included in R). 24 h: fixed 2:1 hit 45% of the time and averaged +0.32R per scenario, Auto hit 59% but gave +0.17R. 3 days: 2:1 – 41% and +0.21R, Auto – 55% and +0.11R. 14 days (with the trend): 2:1 – 39% and +0.16R, Auto – 51% and +0.13R. Conclusion: Auto hits more often because it likes close targets (1:2), but then the win is small. Fixed 2:1 earned the most per scenario, so it is the default. R = profit in units of risk: +0.32R with $10 risk is on average +$3.20 per scenario. Past results do not guarantee future ones.
It’s a statistical and educational tool. Every hour it analyses the charts of about 450 cryptocurrencies from Binance, BingX and OKX and shows how similar chart situations ended in the past – i.e. how often the price went up (LONG) or down (SHORT). Every user sees the same results; they are not tailored to anyone’s situation.
LONG = zarabiasz, gdy cena rośnie. SHORT: LONG = you profit when the price rises. SHORT = you profit when the price falls (available on futures, e.g. BingX or OKX).
Że w podobnych sytuacjach w przeszłości: That in similar past situations the price reached the target first in 45 out of 100 cases, and only then (or never) the stop. It is not a guarantee. Whether 45% is a lot depends on the target type: with 2:1 it is above the break-even threshold (33%), with 1:1 – below it (50%).
Cel (take profit) – poziom ceny zamknięc: Target (take profit) – the price level where you close with a profit. Stop (stop loss) – the level where you close with a loss, limiting further losses. In the app’s statistics both levels are calculated automatically from the coin’s volatility so scenarios can be compared the same way.
Ile możesz zarobić, a ile stracić (2:1,: How much can you win vs. lose (2:1, 1:1, 1:2)?
To stosunek zysku do ryzyka (risk/reward: It’s the reward-to-risk ratio. 2:1 · big win (risk $10 to make $20) – the possible gain is 2× the possible loss; it hits less often (usually 30–45%) but pays off above 33%. 1:1 · even ($10 for $10) – gain = loss, pays off above 50%. 1:2 · small win (risk $10 to make $5) – the gain is half the loss; it hits often (60–80%) but only pays off above 67%. Chance and reward-to-risk always move in opposite directions – that’s maths. What matters is not the percentage itself, but how far it exceeds the break-even threshold.
Matematyczny punkt, przy którym wygrane: The mathematical point where wins and losses balance out (33% for 2:1, 50% for 1:1, 67% for 1:2). “Above threshold” means the historical statistic of the scenario was higher than this point. Past results do not guarantee future results.

Dla każdego coina bierzemy mocniejszy sc: For each coin we take the stronger scenario (LONG or SHORT) for the chosen horizon and target type. Then we order the list in three groups: 1) scenarios that clearly passed the test on the coin’s history, are above the break-even threshold and have an edge over normal of at least +8 pts for 24 h and 3 days (+5 pts for 14 days) – in the test on the history of over 100 coins this rule gave about 49–51% hits with 2:1, 2) other scenarios that passed the test (below threshold, smaller edge or only a borderline pass), 3) coins with a warning (chart says nothing, coin too new, extreme move, single-trend history, low volume). Within each group the edge over normal decides: how many percentage points the chance is now above normal for this coin. E.g. a coin that normally hits 27% and now 40% (+13 pts) ranks above a coin at 38% with a normal of 36% (+2 pts) – because here the current chart really changes something. Bo procent nie odpowiada na pytanie „czy: Because the percentage doesn’t answer “will the price rise?”, but: will the price reach a specific target BEFORE touching the stop, within the given time. The trend can continue and the price can still hit the stop along the way. Also, with 2:1 the target is far, so it rarely hits – 30–40% is normal and the threshold is 33%. Finally, the statistic comes from that coin’s history: if in similar setups the price more often reversed than continued, the percentage will be low despite the trend. When the percentage “disagrees” with the trend, the coin details show a box explaining it for that coin.
Czy aplikacja kieruje się średnią kroczą: Does the app follow the moving average?
Częściowo. Średnia krocząca (EMA 50 i na: Partly. The moving average (EMA 50 and the EMA 20 slope) is only some of the factors. The others are RSI, volume, buy pressure, volume delta (CVD), the price position in its 20-candle range, and for 24 h and 3 days also the Bitcoin trend (the whole market) and – for 24 h – the 4h trend. The model has no fixed rule like “price below average = sell” – it checks how similar combinations of all factors ended in that coin’s history. So the result depends on the coin’s past, not just on the chart of the last few days.
Średnia krocząca (EMA 50) działa jak „li: The moving average (EMA 50) works like a “trend line”: price above it = uptrend, below = downtrend. A trend break is a candle closing on the other side of that line. The card in the coin details shows how often in this coin’s history – in a similar chart setup – a break happened within the given time, and at what price the average sits. The further the price is from the average (e.g. right after a big pump), the smaller the chance of a break in a short time. A break does not mean the price will keep going the new way – it signals that the current trend is weakening.
Gdy coin w całej swojej historii np. kil: If a coin grew several-fold over its whole history, the model “learned” that it usually rises. If the price is now clearly falling, such situations barely exist in the data – the statistic looks in the rear-view mirror and may disagree with the chart. So we show a warning and move the coin to the end of the TOP 10. The same works the other way (a coin that mostly fell and is now rising).
Coin zmienił cenę o 40% lub więcej w 24h: The coin moved 40% or more in 24h (a sharp rise or drop). In such situations history describes poorly what is happening, so the statistic is unreliable and volatility and risk are exceptionally high.
24 godz. – krótki trading, szybkie ruchy: 24 h – short-term trading, fast moves, more randomness. 3 days – swing, a good compromise. 14 days – longer positions, bigger moves in percent. The percentage is not necessarily higher for longer horizons – more time also means a bigger move needed to reach the target.

Średnia krocząca (EMA 50) działa jak „li: The moving average (EMA 50) works like a “trend line”: price above it = uptrend, below it = downtrend. A trend break is a candle closing on the other side of that line. The average does not stand still – every candle it moves towards the price. After a strong rise, when the price starts to stall, the average quickly catches up and the break happens without a big drop. So a high chance of a break does NOT mean a high chance for a SHORT – more often it simply means the trend is weakening and the price is no longer running away from the average.
